question: Does median PM2.5 differ between seasons when the same cities are compared?
unit: city (median of daily values per season)
interpretation: Across 324 cities, p < 0.001 (below α); Kendall's W = 0.64 (large agreement in seasonal ranking). Highest median season: Post-monsoon (75.5 µg/m³); lowest: Monsoon (50.7 µg/m³). 10 of 10 pairwise season contrasts remain below α after Holm correction.

question: Do city-level median PM2.5 values differ between province groups?
interpretation: 4 groups, 322 cities: H = 111.10, p < 0.001 (below α); ε² = 0.34 (large). 5 of 6 pairwise contrasts below α after Holm.

question: Do mean city-level PM2.5 values differ between province groups?
interpretation: ANOVA not reported because its assumptions are not reasonably met: normality rejected (Shapiro–Wilk p < 0.05) in: Balochistan, Punjab, Sindh; equal variances rejected (Levene p = 0.000626). Use the Kruskal–Wallis result instead.

question: Within cities, is mean PM2.5 different on weekdays than on weekends?
interpretation: Median weekday−weekend difference = -0.23 µg/m³ (95 % bootstrap CI -0.30 to -0.16), i.e. -0.3 % of the typical weekend level; p < 0.001 (below α); rank-biserial = -0.40 (moderate consistency across cities). The difference is consistent but very small in absolute terms; statistical significance here does not imply practical importance.
